doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Opening, and how Monk and Zoot got their nicknames
summary: Rowe introduces the session at Hotel Utica; Appleyard asks how he got the name Monk, and they trade the story of Zoot Sims's nickname from a music stand.

Peter Appleyard is one of the most respected of all Canadian musicians, and has been performing on vibes and drums from his home base of Toronto since the 1950s. He was born in Grimsby, England, on August 26, 1928. His long career has included associations with Benny Goodman, Bucky Pizzarelli, Dick Hyman, and Frank Sinatra.
Peter was interviewed in Utica, NY, on October 4, 2012, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and I’m here at the Hotel Utica with vibist Peter Appleyard. Welcome to Utica.
Thanks, Monk. Before we go any further, how did you get the name Monk?
Aha! You’ve turned the tables on me. Actually it was because of a big, long, blue coat I used to wear, with a hood on it.
And someone said, “You look like a Monk with that thing on.” And it stuck.
That’s similar to the moniker that Zoot Sims adopted.
How did he get that, do you know?

Well I think he was playing in this school band and they had the music stands, they were old music stands, and they had the names of the guys on the music stands. And they were either their real name or a pseudonym or whatever. And his said, “Zoot.” It stayed with him.
